ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The battery of an electric vehicle can provide a voltage of $48\mathrm{V}$, with negligible internal resistance. The total mass when a person rides on it is $100\mathrm{kg}$. When the electric vehicle is moving at a constant speed of $8\mathrm{m/s}$ on a horizontal ground, the current through the motor is $5\mathrm{A}$. The resistance experienced by the electric vehicle is always $0.025$ times the total weight of the vehicle and the person. The friction of the electric vehicle itself is ignored, and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Find the resistance $R$ of the electric motor.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The battery of an electric vehicle can provide a voltage of $48\mathrm{V}$, with negligible internal resistance. The total mass when a person rides on it is $100\mathrm{kg}$. When the electric vehicle is moving at a constant speed of $8\mathrm{m/s}$ on a horizontal ground, the current through the motor is $5\mathrm{A}$. The resistance experienced by the electric vehicle is always $0.025$ times the total weight of the vehicle and the person. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Use power balance. Given U = 48 V, I = 5 A, m = 100 kg, v = 8 m/s, g = 10 m/s^2. The external resistance force is 0.025 times the total weight: F = 0.025mg = 0.025 × 100 × 10 = 25 N. Since the vehicle moves at constant speed on horizontal ground, the useful mechanical output power equals the power needed to overcome this resistance: P_mech = Fv = 25 × 8 = 200 W. The electrical input power from the battery is P_in = UI = 48 × 5 = 240 W. The difference is the heat loss in the motor winding: P_loss = P_in − P_mech = 240 − 200 = 40 W. Since P_loss = I^2R, the motor resistance is R = 40 / 5^2 = 40 / 25 = 1.6 Ω.

method.method_draft: Use the motor back-emf route. From the text, read U = 48 V, I = 5 A, m = 100 kg, v = 8 m/s, resistance force coefficient 0.025, and g = 10 m/s^2. First find the road resistance force: F = 0.025mg = 25 N. Since the vehicle moves at constant speed, the motor’s mechanical power output is Fv = 25 × 8 = 200 W. In a DC motor model, mechanical output power is supplied through the back emf, so P_mech = EI. Hence E = P_mech/I = 200/5 = 40 V. With negligible battery internal resistance, the terminal voltage satisfies U = E + IR. Therefore R = (U − E)/I = (48 − 40)/5 = 1.6 Ω.
